facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The critical edition prepared by the Oriental Institute of Baroda establishes the authentic verses of Valmiki's text, omitting later regional interpolations.
facts.source_name: Oriental Institute, Baroda (Critical Edition of Valmiki Ramayana)
facts.text: The critical edition of the Sanskrit Valmiki Ramayana contains no mention of Ravana capturing Shani or using him as a staircase to mount his throne.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: According to popular legend, Ravana captured the Navagrahas and made them lie down as steps to his throne.
facts.text: Popular Indian folklore recounts that Ravana subdued all nine planetary deities and forced them to lie face down at the foot of his throne to serve as living stairs.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Enraged that Shani moved a leg into the twelfth house to prevent Meghanada's absolute immortality, Ravana struck his leg, causing Shani's limp.
facts.text: A prevalent mythological tale claims Ravana fractured Shani's leg after the deity shifted into the twelfth house to prevent Meghanada from gaining absolute immortality.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Narada suggested that stepping on their chests would show greater supremacy, prompting Ravana to flip them and receive Shani's ill-omened gaze.
facts.text: Folk narrations state that sage Narada tricked Ravana into turning the imprisoned planets face up, thereby exposing the king to Shani's devastating direct glance.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Ananda Ramayana is a 15th-century Sanskrit text that narrates traditions including the captivity of planetary deities in Lanka.
facts.text: The Ananda Ramayana, a Sanskrit text composed around the 15th century CE, incorporates post-Valmiki traditions featuring Ravana's imprisonment of the planetary deities beneath his throne.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Graha digpal bibas narahi — all planets and directional guardians were subjugated by Ravana's prowess.
facts.text: In the 16th-century epic Ramcharitmanas, Tulsidas metaphorically notes that all planetary gods and guardians bowed to Ravana's might, but makes no mention of Shani being used as a physical staircase.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: On the lines of the investigations carried out in the Mahabharata sites, Lal commenced on another project in 1975 titled, Archaeology of the Ramayana sites.
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India initiated the major excavation project titled 'Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites' in 1975 under Director General B. B. Lal.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The excavations at Sringaverapura exposed a massive burnt-brick tank measuring more than 250 metres in length, datable to the turn of the Christian era.
facts.text: Excavations by the Archaeological Survey of India at the Ramayana-related site of Sringaverapura revealed a large burnt-brick tank system measuring more than 250 metres in length.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Excavations at Bharadvaja Asrama revealed stratified deposits extending from the Northern Black Polished Ware period.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Memoir No. 103)
facts.text: Excavations at the Bharadvaja Ashrama site in Prayagraj by the Archaeological Survey of India uncovered stratified occupation layers dating back to the Northern Black Polished Ware period around 700 BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The lintels and sculptural panels of the Gupta period at Deogarh illustrate the architectural integration of the planetary deities.
facts.text: Surveys by the Archaeological Survey of India of the 5th-century CE Gupta-period Dashavatara Temple in Deogarh confirmed early architectural relief carvings featuring standardized planetary deities in Hindu temple art.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Sankalia argued on archaeological and geographical grounds that Ravana's Lanka lay in eastern Madhya Pradesh rather than the island of Sri Lanka.
facts.source_name: H. D. Sankalia, 'Ramayana: Myth or Reality?'
facts.text: Archaeologist H. D. Sankalia argued that geographical descriptions in the earliest layers of the Ramayana place Ravana's Lanka in central India near the Vindhyas, while mainstream traditions and other researchers locate it on the island of Sri Lanka.
